project.one_liner: A daily devotional app: one short reading, one reflection prompt and a quiet moment, in under five minutes.

objective: Launch an identity that makes a daily devotional habit feel calm and personal rather than preachy, and stands out from meditation apps.

audiences.name: Adults with a faith practice who want a short daily routine
audiences.context: On their phone, early morning or before sleep, often alone
audiences.must_believe: This will take five minutes and leave me calmer, not lectured.

audiences.name: People returning to a practice after a long break
audiences.context: Curious but wary of feeling judged
audiences.must_believe: I can start again here without explaining myself.

positioning.problem: Devotional content online is either dense and text-heavy or styled like a generic meditation app.
positioning.promise: A quiet five minutes that fits a real morning.
proof: One reading and one prompt a day, no feed

persona_test: Would a tired parent opening this at 6:40 before the kids wake up feel calmer within one screen?

surfaces.name: App icon and app store listing

must_include: Readable text at default phone sizes

assumptions: Mobile app is the first surface; website and social come later
Content is in English at launch

open_questions.question: Which launch markets, and is any translation planned for year one?
Should the identity signal a specific tradition or stay broadly spiritual?
What makes this different from scripture apps beyond tone? The differentiator is still blank.
Has 'Aurel' been through a trademark search in the app and software classes?

missing: Tradition question answered (directions can still start)
List of product features and their release state
